control.basis: Raise the hood 8 mm, as a mislocated hood mount would, so it squeezes the FUEL beyond the launch trial's indentation in the wrap

objectives.objective: AUTO: start with up to eight supported FUEL and score from a legal launch pose while the HUB is active
objectives.basis: The starting fold holds 37 or more FUEL by free volume (start-capacity premise); the launch and flight cases carry a FUEL into the HUB opening from the 2.7 m pose that the re-run rehearsal credits in AUTO (delivery-pose premise). With Agent FRC 0.84 wait-cycle yield and the shared partner deconfliction, delivering from 2.70 m costs no FUEL: slot 2 credits 124 in both the baseline and R3 series (alliance totals 366 and 382). Pre-0.84 results (96 against 104) were understated by permanent wait cycles.

objectives.objective: Inactive shift: collect and hold the next allocated stock from the DEPOT, OUTPOST or a partner
objectives.basis: The acquire cases take a floor FUEL up the bumper face and over the bumper along the acquisition trial's trace (captured in 0.53 s); the hopper cases follow the entry trial from capture to rest against the stopped flywheel (3.0 s, floor belts stopped). hopper-capacity is 38 or more by free volume. The entry trial is one FUEL in an empty lane: a batch of 24 collected onto stopped belts is not evaluated, and a running belt wedges the FUEL into the stopped pinch (entry-floor-belt-running trials).

objectives.objective: Active shift: carry each FUEL from storage through one transfer into the HUB
objectives.basis: loaded-transit, the launch cases and the flight cases carry the tracked FUEL from its seat into the HUB cavity along the launch and delivery trials' traces. The launch trial backs the FUEL off the stopped wheel, spins the wheel up and feeds it; it releases at 6.86 m/s and 61.9 degrees, and the delivery trials score from 6.70 to 7.00 m/s.

objectives.objective: Active shift: sustain 2.00 FUEL/s to score 24 with stock ready by second 5
objectives.basis: Two pinch lanes. If every FUEL moved at the 0.6 m/s belt speed with 154 mm spacing, each lane would feed 3.9 FUEL/s. The launch trial's single free FUEL rolls on that belt at 0.22 m/s from rest (mean over the feed), which is 1.4 FUEL/s per lane and 2.8 for two lanes against 2.00, so the margin depends on how a stacked batch rides the belt. The launch trial's wheel does 28 J of work per FUEL at the imposed speed. A free 0.006 kg m2 wheel would lose 6.8% of its speed supplying it, against a scoring band of plus or minus 2.2%, so the wheel's inertia or its speed control has to carry the shot (gate G5). The first FUEL of a batch takes 2.3 s from its seat to release (back-off, spin-up, feed). Bulk convergence and the sustained rate are gate G1. Verification gates are in verification-gates.json; the contract assigns physical performance, retention and actuator dynamics to their own commissioned evidence (docs/preliminary-design.md).

objectives.objective: Fallback: score the available batch when supply or traffic consumes the window and return to collecting
objectives.basis: The cycle is piece-count independent; the intake stays deployed in every operating case; the re-run rehearsal keeps the depot loop.

objectives.objective: Traffic: remain in the own zone, keep possession through loaded driving and contact, and yield
objectives.basis: By geometry the front lip stands 61 mm above the floor belts, so by statics a floor FUEL needs about 5.2 g of horizontal deceleration to roll over it; side and rear walls rise above the top layer; the open throat holds no counted FUEL. The seated FUEL is held only by the stopped flywheel behind it and friction: nothing restrains it forward during the loaded transit. Loaded 0.5 g stops are gate G2. Verification gates are in verification-gates.json; the contract assigns physical performance, retention and actuator dynamics to their own commissioned evidence (docs/preliminary-design.md).

objectives.objective: Neutral collector alternative with two field crossings
objectives.basis: The coordinator selected the own-zone role. R3 keeps a BUMP crossing option (bump-crossing premise, 8.7 mm least clearance) with the intake retracted; the re-run TRENCH variant (R3L) credits fewer FUEL than the depot loop.

objectives.objective: End game: Level 1 low-rung hang when its expected 10 points exceed the remaining FUEL service
objectives.basis: Cases reach, seat (2 mm required contact) and lift 70 mm; the 714 mm frame gives 23.9 mm of bumper overlap with each upright (hang-bumper-overlap premise); the hang physics trial at 70.3 kg holds 37.5 mm with the brake and fails without it; its cable load peaks at 1043 N in the lift and settles at 690 N. Jaw capture under lateral offset and the brake hold are gate G3. Verification gates are in verification-gates.json; the contract assigns physical performance, retention and actuator dynamics to their own commissioned evidence (docs/preliminary-design.md).

objectives.objective: AUTO Level 1 TOWER (15 points, two-robot cap)
objectives.basis: The strategy keeps the eight-FUEL AUTO objective; no joined AUTO climb evidence is sought in this layout.

objectives.objective: Reserve the depot entrance and partner lane
objectives.basis: Alliance routing decision owned by the field rehearsal, independent of the robot layout.

objectives.objective: Measurement: observe intake crossing, retained identity, release and downstream crossing on one timebase
objectives.basis: entry sensor at the front lip and pinch sensor at the flywheel lane are placed; the HUB counter is field equipment.

flywheel.purpose: Stop the entering FUEL while it is at rest, then accelerate the FUEL against the hood.

The wheel-to-hood gap is the FUEL diameter less 12 mm, so the stopped wheel is the seat stop and the spinning wheel grips: the launch trial releases at 6.86 m/s from a 13.4 m/s surface. The launch trial's wheel does 28 J of work per FUEL at the imposed speed. presentation.title: Floor-fed hooded flywheel shooter
presentation.focus: FUEL tracked: The mission cases follow this FUEL from the carpet into the HUB.
notes: What it is: the R3-PD2 whole-robot preliminary blockout (tall floor-fed hooded-flywheel shooter on a 680 x 714 mm four-module swerve base). Solids are planning envelopes and simplified material blocks, not a Fusion robot.

Simplified: swerve modules are body, motor and azimuth envelopes; electronics are two panel blocks; belts and rollers are rigid outlines; the HUB and TOWER are V0-dimension fixtures, not the official field model. The intake belt, top roller, flywheel and hood are drawn at the squeeze the physics trials use (dimensions.py), so the tracked FUEL overlaps them by the trial's indentation; each such pair is declared as payload compression in its case.

Tracked FUEL motion: every one of its 28 cases is a stroke fitted within 1.50 mm (limit 1.5 mm) to the solved acquire, entry, launch and deliver trials in field-trials.json. Each stroke is uniform in its own parameter, so playback timing inside a case is not the trial's; the trial window is in caseTimes. Contact stiffness, damping, friction and rolling resistance are estimates, not measurements, and no FUEL force-deflection curve is available.

Imposed in the trials: robot approach speed, intake belt speed (3.0 m/s), the floor belt schedule (stopped during entry; 0.3 m/s back-off, then 0.6 m/s feed) and the flywheel surface speed (13.4 m/s). Whether the motors sustain them under load is not solved.
Prescribed, not simulated, in the package: the intake slide, the field moving in the robot frame (transit and TOWER approach), and the climb strokes.
Unverified: verification gates G1-G7 (verification-gates.json) carry the physical tests; hopper capacity is a free-volume premise; dynamic BUMP crossing and robot-to-robot contact are not evaluated.

Sources and cutoff: FRC REBUILT kickoff manual V0 with Team Update 00, cutoff 2026-01-10 23:59:59 America/New_York (construction-rules.json); field dimensions from the V0 description (geometry.py field_bodies).
Open items: see openItems.

Open item: No hold-back for the seated FUEL. Nothing restrains the seated FUEL forward. Without the belt's back-off, a FUEL at rest 0.23 mm into the stopped wheel still launches at speed and one 0.44 mm in is fed early at spin-up; that threshold comes from the penalty contact springing a lightly pressed FUEL clear and is not a measured limit. With the back-off a FUEL pressed 3.2 mm in launches at speed; one wedged 5.9 mm in by a running belt does not. No hold-back is designed.

Open item: Batch collection is not evaluated: the entry trial is one FUEL in an empty lane with the floor belts stopped; a running belt wedges the FUEL into the stopped pinch (entry-floor-belt-running trials).
Open item: Feed rate: a free FUEL rolls at about a third of the belt speed in the launch trial, so the sustained 2.00 FUEL/s objective rests on gate G1, not on the belt-speed calculation.

Open item: Launch inputs are imposed: flywheel surface speed, belt schedule and the squeeze. The wheel does 28 J of work per FUEL in the trial, a 6.8% speed drop for a free 0.006 kg m2 wheel, which the trial does not apply. Motor sizing and the FUEL's force-deflection curve are not measured.

Open item: The seat position depends on contact damping, which is an estimate: at damping ratio 0.3 the FUEL rests against the wheel; at 0.20 and 0.10 it rebounds and rests 7 and 62 mm clear of it (still seated, and the launch from there still scores, later). Rest time is 3.0 s; it needed a 0.05 ms timestep to converge.
Open item: Contact stiffness is an estimate and decides the launch: 10 and 30 kN/m score, 7.5 kN/m releases too slowly. The 8 to 16 mm squeeze bracket is a force bracket at 15 kN/m.

Open item: Scoring band: only 6.70 to 7.00 m/s scores at the nominal drag and spin lift and at all four corners. 6.55 m/s misses at the high-drag, high-spin corner and 7.15 m/s at both low-drag corners. The band's ends score off the HUB top plate or cavity wall; the point-mass screen's clean band at this release is narrower (package-facts.json shot.pointMassBands in the experiment folder).
Open item: Intake belt load: the acquisition trial's contacts dissipate up to 786 W at the imposed 3 m/s, above the intake's 30 A supply limit; the trial fails at 2.0 m/s.

Open item: A carrier-free FUEL stroke (carpet approach, free flight, rolling on stopped belts) has no evidence slot in the layout schema; its trial window is recorded in the case basis and in caseTimes.
Open item: No registered structure-to-frame joint: hopper walls (hopper front upper wall, hopper rear wall, hopper wall left, hopper wall right).
Open item: No registered structure-to-frame joint: climber tubes and winch (climber tube left, climber tube right, climber winch) to the climber tube mounts.
Open item: Frame-internal joints are not registered: frame rails, floor pan, floor pan front tongue, front lip, climber tube mounts and intake slide rails.
Open item: Battery hold-down strap over the battery top is undesigned; the cleats capture it in X only.
Open item: Group-level mount datums: right-hand members (climber hook right, climber inner tube right, intake carriage plate right, shooter side plate right) cite the left-hand datum.
